questions.title: Up the Ladder
questions.story_md:
Who does crew member **{member}** ultimately answer to?

Return **id**, **name** and **level** for the member (level 0), their boss (level 1), the boss's boss (level 2) … up to the top.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(id, name, boss_id, level) AS (SELECT id, name, boss_id, 0 FROM crew WHERE id = {member} UNION ALL SELECT c.id, c.name, c.boss_id, up.level + 1 FROM crew c JOIN up ON c.id = up.boss_id) SELECT id, name, level FROM up;

hints.text: WITH RECURSIVE: start at the member, then join to the boss.
Stop is automatic when boss_id is NULL.

questions.title: Whole Team
questions.story_md:
Turn crew member **{boss}** and you get their whole team.

Return **id** and **name** of member {boss} **and everyone who reports to them directly or indirectly**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE team(id) AS (SELECT {boss} UNION ALL SELECT c.id FROM crew c JOIN team t ON c.boss_id = t.id) SELECT c.id, c.name FROM crew c JOIN team t ON t.id = c.id;

hints.text: Seed the recursion with direct reports, then add their reports.

questions.title: Org Depth
questions.story_md:
Map the whole hierarchy.

Return **id** and **depth** of every crew member (members with no boss have depth 0).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE d(id, depth) AS (SELECT id, 0 FROM crew WHERE boss_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.id, d.depth + 1 FROM crew c JOIN d ON c.boss_id = d.id) SELECT id, depth FROM d;

hints.text: Start from roots (boss_id IS NULL) and walk down.

questions.title: Team Payout
questions.story_md:
What does boss **{boss}**'s whole operation cost?

Return two numbers: the **number of people** in the team **including the boss**, and their **total cut**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE crew (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, boss_id INTEGER, cut INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE team(id) AS (SELECT {boss} UNION ALL SELECT c.id FROM crew c JOIN team t ON c.boss_id = t.id) SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(c.cut) FROM crew c JOIN team t ON t.id = c.id;

hints.text: Recursive team, then aggregate.

questions.title: Every Single Day
questions.story_md:
Guards notice patterns, including quiet days.

For the **14 days** starting **{start}**, return each **day** and the **number of alarms** that day — days without alarms must show **0**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE days(day) AS (SELECT {start|sql} UNION ALL SELECT date(day, '+1 day') FROM days WHERE day < date({start|sql}, '+13 days')) SELECT d.day, COUNT(a.id) FROM days d LEFT JOIN alarms a ON a.triggered = d.day GROUP BY d.day;

hints.text: Generate dates with date(day, '+1 day').
LEFT JOIN alarms and COUNT(a.id).

questions.title: Tunnel Network
questions.story_md:
Tunnels connect zones (one-way, `from_zone` → `to_zone`).

Return every **zone reachable** from **{zone}** and the **fewest tunnels** needed to get there — include **{zone}** itself with **0**. Watch out for loops; no route needs more than 8 tunnels.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE tunnels (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, from_zone TEXT, to_zone TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH RECURSIVE r(zone, steps) AS (SELECT {zone|sql}, 0 UNION SELECT t.to_zone, r.steps + 1 FROM tunnels t JOIN r ON t.from_zone = r.zone WHERE r.steps < 8) SELECT zone, MIN(steps) FROM r GROUP BY zone;

hints.text: Carry a step counter and stop at 8 so cycles end.
GROUP BY zone with MIN(steps).

questions.title: Work Streaks
questions.story_md:
Find employee **{emp}**'s streaks of consecutive working days in March.

Count each day once (they may have several shifts a day). Return **start day**, **end day** and **length** (days) of every streak.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM shifts WHERE employee_id = {emp}), g AS (SELECT day, julianday(day) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY day) AS grp FROM d) SELECT MIN(day), MAX(day), COUNT(*) FROM g GROUP BY grp;

hints.text: Consecutive dates minus their row number give the same value.
GROUP BY that value.

questions.title: Iron Man
questions.story_md:
Who never takes a day off?

For every employee with shifts, return **employee_id** and the **length of their longest streak** of consecutive working days.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT employee_id, day FROM shifts), g AS (SELECT employee_id, julianday(day) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY day) AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS len FROM g GROUP BY employee_id, grp) SELECT employee_id, MAX(len) FROM s GROUP BY employee_id;

hints.text: Same islands trick, partitioned by employee.
Then take the MAX streak.

questions.title: Days Off
questions.story_md:
When is employee **{emp}** away?

Return **first day off** and **last day off** for every gap between two of their working days in March (a gap is one or more days with no shift).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM shifts WHERE employee_id = {emp}), n AS (SELECT day, LEAD(day) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS next_day FROM d) SELECT date(day, '+1 day'), date(next_day, '-1 day') FROM n WHERE julianday(next_day) - julianday(day) > 1;

hints.text: LEAD gives the next working day; a gap exists when they are > 1 day apart.

questions.title: Escalations
questions.story_md:
In zone **{zone}**, alarms come in runs of the same level.

Ordering the zone's alarms by **triggered, then id**, group **consecutive alarms with the same level** into runs. Return **level**, the **id of the first alarm** in the run and the **run length**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT id, level, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY triggered, id) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY level ORDER BY triggered, id) AS grp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY triggered, id) AS pos FROM alarms WHERE zone = {zone|sql}) SELECT level, (SELECT id FROM o o2 WHERE o2.level = o.level AND o2.grp = o.grp ORDER BY pos LIMIT 1), COUNT(*) FROM o GROUP BY level, grp;

hints.text: Row number overall minus row number per level is constant within a run.

questions.title: Restless Zones
questions.story_md:
A streak is a run of consecutive days on which a zone raised at least one alarm.

For every zone return **zone**, the **number of streaks** and the **longest streak** (days).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT zone, triggered AS day FROM alarms), g AS (SELECT zone, julianday(day) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY day) AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT zone, COUNT(*) AS len FROM g GROUP BY zone, grp) SELECT zone, COUNT(*), MAX(len) FROM s GROUP BY zone;

hints.text: Islands per zone, then count them and take the longest.

questions.title: Top Earners
questions.story_md:
Each department's top **{n}** earners have the codes.

Return **dept**, **first_name** and **salary** for the top {n} per department (highest salary first; ties broken by lower id).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT dept, first_name, salary FROM (SELECT dept, first_name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC, id) AS rn FROM employees) WHERE rn <= {n};

hints.text: ROW_NUMBER per department, then keep rn <= n.

questions.title: Best in Show
questions.story_md:
One item per zone — the best one.

Return **zone**, **tag** and **value** of the most valuable item in each zone (ties: lower id).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, tag, value FROM (SELECT zone, tag, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY value DESC, id) AS rn FROM vault_items) WHERE rn = 1;

hints.text: Top-1 per group with ROW_NUMBER.

questions.title: Favourite Shops
questions.story_md:
Where does each target shop most?

For each account, return **account_id**, **merchant** and **total spent** for its **top 2 merchants** by total amount (ignore missing merchants; ties: merchant name A→Z).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT account_id, merchant, SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE merchant IS NOT NULL GROUP BY account_id, merchant) SELECT account_id, merchant, total FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY total DESC, merchant) AS rn FROM m) WHERE rn <= 2;

hints.text: Aggregate first, then rank inside each account.

questions.title: Joint Winners
questions.story_md:
Best-paid person in each branch — and if there is a tie, all of them.

Return **branch_id**, **first_name** and **salary** of everyone with the **highest salary in their branch**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT branch_id, first_name, salary FROM (SELECT branch_id, first_name, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY branch_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees) WHERE r = 1;

hints.text: RANK (not ROW_NUMBER) keeps ties.

questions.title: Fresh Tracks
questions.story_md:
The latest movements per zone matter most.

Return **zone**, **log id** and **at** of the **{n} most recent** log entries in each zone (latest date first; same date → higher id first).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, id, at FROM (SELECT zone, id, at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY at DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM vault_logs) WHERE rn <= {n};

hints.text: Order DESC inside the window, keep rn <= n.

questions.title: Threat Board
questions.story_md:
One row per zone, one column per alarm level.

Return **zone**, and the counts of **low**, **medium**, **high** and **critical** alarms (in that column order, 0 if none).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, SUM(CASE WHEN level = 'low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN level = 'medium' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN level = 'high' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN level = 'critical' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM alarms GROUP BY zone;

hints.text: SUM(CASE WHEN level = … THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) per column.

questions.title: Monthly Ledger
questions.story_md:
A spreadsheet the boss can read.

Return **month** (`YYYY-MM`) and the total amounts of **deposit**, **withdrawal** and **transfer** transactions that month (in that column order, 0 if none).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', at), SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'transfer' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) FROM transactions GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', at);

hints.text: Group by month; one conditional SUM per kind.

questions.title: Rota
questions.story_md:
Who works which shift?

Return **employee_id** and how many **morning**, **day**, **evening** and **night** shifts they worked (that column order; only employees with shifts).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT employee_id, SUM(shift = 'morning'), SUM(shift = 'day'), SUM(shift = 'evening'), SUM(shift = 'night') FROM shifts GROUP BY employee_id;

hints.text: In SQLite a comparison is 1 or 0, so SUM(shift = …) counts.

questions.title: Account Matrix
questions.story_md:
Rows are account types, columns are statuses.

Return **type** and the number of **active**, **frozen** and **closed** accounts (that column order).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT type, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'frozen' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'closed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM accounts GROUP BY type;

hints.text: One CASE column per status.

questions.title: Spending Spree
questions.story_md:
Someone suddenly spends more — maybe a bribe.

Return **account_id**, **H1 total** (Jan–Jun 2025) and **H2 total** (Jul–Dec 2025) of **withdrawal** amounts for accounts whose H2 total is **at least {pct}% higher** than H1 (only accounts with withdrawals in both halves).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH h1 AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) AS t FROM transactions WHERE kind = 'withdrawal' AND at < '2025-07-01' GROUP BY account_id), h2 AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) AS t FROM transactions WHERE kind = 'withdrawal' AND at >= '2025-07-01' GROUP BY account_id) SELECT h1.account_id, h1.t, h2.t FROM h1 JOIN h2 ON h2.account_id = h1.account_id WHERE h2.t >= h1.t * (1 + {pct} / 100.0);

hints.text: One CTE per half-year, then JOIN them.

questions.title: Payroll Share
questions.story_md:
Which department costs the most?

Return **dept**, **total salary**, its **share of the whole payroll in % (2 decimals)** and its **rank** by total (largest = 1).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH d AS (SELECT dept, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY dept), g AS (SELECT SUM(total) AS grand FROM d) SELECT dept, total, ROUND(100.0 * total / grand, 2), RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total DESC) FROM d, g;

hints.text: A CTE for per-dept totals and another for the grand total.

questions.title: Inside Job
questions.story_md:
Suspicious: being in a zone on a day it raised an alarm.

Return **employee_id** and the **number of distinct (zone, day) matches** for employees with **at least {n}** such matches.
questions.reference_sql: WITH hits AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.employee_id, l.zone, l.at FROM vault_logs l JOIN alarms a ON a.zone = l.zone AND a.triggered = l.at) SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) FROM hits GROUP BY employee_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= {n};

hints.text: Match logs to alarms on zone and date, de-duplicate, then count.

questions.title: Branch Health
questions.story_md:
A branch report card.

For every branch id with accounts, return **branch_id**, **number of accounts**, **average balance (2 decimals)** and **% frozen (2 decimals)**, but only for branches where **more than {pct}%** of accounts are frozen.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT branch_id, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(balance) AS avg_balance, SUM(status = 'frozen') AS frozen FROM accounts GROUP BY branch_id) SELECT branch_id, n, ROUND(avg_balance, 2), ROUND(100.0 * frozen / n, 2) FROM s WHERE 100.0 * frozen / n > {pct};

hints.text: Compute counts once, then derive the ratios.

questions.title: Shop of the Month
questions.story_md:
Where did the money go each month?

Return **month** (`YYYY-MM`), the **merchant with the highest total amount** that month and that **total** (ignore missing merchants; ties: merchant name A→Z).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', at) AS month, merchant, SUM(amount) AS total FROM transactions WHERE merchant IS NOT NULL GROUP BY month, merchant), r AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY month ORDER BY total DESC, merchant) AS rn FROM m) SELECT month, merchant, total FROM r WHERE rn = 1;

hints.text: Totals per (month, merchant), rank within month, keep rank 1.

questions.title: The Middle
questions.story_md:
Averages lie; medians don't.

Return **dept** and the **median salary** (2 decimals). For an even count, the median is the average of the two middle salaries.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT dept, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY dept) AS n FROM employees) SELECT dept, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM o WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY dept;

hints.text: Number rows within the dept and keep the middle one(s).
Integer division: (n+1)/2 and (n+2)/2.

questions.title: Percentile
questions.story_md:
How rare is each item in zone **{zone}**?

Return **tag**, **value** and its **CUME_DIST** by value ascending (fraction of items with value ≤ this one), rounded to 3 decimals.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT tag, value, ROUND(CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY value), 3) FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY value)

questions.title: Above the Line
questions.story_md:
Compare everyone to their peers without a GROUP BY.

Return **id**, **dept**, **salary** and **salary minus the department average** (2 decimals), using a window function.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, dept, salary, ROUND(salary - AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept), 2) FROM employees;

hints.text: AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept) keeps every row.

questions.title: Crown of the Zone
questions.story_md:
Each item next to its zone's crown jewel.

Return **zone**, **tag**, **value** and the **tag of the most valuable item in the same zone** (ties: lower id).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT zone, tag, value, FIRST_VALUE(tag) OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY value DESC, id) FROM vault_items;

hints.text: FIRST_VALUE(tag) OVER (PARTITION BY zone ORDER BY value DESC, id)

questions.title: Hot Week
questions.story_md:
Is zone **{zone}** heating up?

For each of its alarms, return **id**, **triggered** and the **number of alarms in that zone during the 7 days ending on that date** (that date and the 6 before; same-day alarms all count).
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE alarms (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone TEXT, level TEXT, triggered TEXT, minutes INTEGER, resolved INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, triggered, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY julianday(triggered) RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM alarms WHERE zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: RANGE works on the ORDER BY value: order by julianday(triggered).
RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
